attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation depends on Yang-Mills analytic inputs not yet proved: existence of the finite boundary decomposition N=\Gamma\circ M+A for renormalized Wilson products, positivity or covariance interpretation of the separate A and \Gamma pieces, and a no-new-boundary-renormalization theorem showing that after individual Wilson renormalizations the normalized mixed anomaly is rank one or trivial. Without those estimates, the linear-algebra argument is valid but not yet a proof for four-dimensional Yang-Mills.
steps: Start with regulated reflection positivity: for every cutoff and collar, the finite matrix N^{a,L,\delta}_{ij}=S_{a,L}(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j) is positive semidefinite.

Use the RG-to-OS interface topology only on fixed-collar reflected probes. Entrywise convergence gives N^\delta\ge0 in the continuum; then the finite-dimensional closed cone gives N=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}N^\delta\ge0 whenever the collar limit exists.

Compare N with the intended time-zero OS matrix M_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i,F_j). The most general finite obstruction seen in previous cycles is N=\Gamma\circ M+A: multiplicative Wilson/cusp factors in \Gamma and additive plane-supported contacts in A.

Apply diagonal trace locking. Since individual observables are already identified with the same continuum theory, N_{ii}=M_{ii}; after absorbing allowed individual Wilson renormalizations, this sets \Gamma_{ii}=1 and A_{ii}=0.

If A is a positive boundary-contact matrix, Cauchy-Schwarz for positive matrices gives |A_{ij}|^2\le A_{ii}A_{jj}=0, hence A=0. Thus a surviving additive mixed contact cannot be a positive covariance compatible with diagonal trace continuity; it is itself a falsifier of positive boundary OPE compatibility.

With A=0, recover the intended matrix by M=\Gamma^{[-1]}\circ N. A topology-level positivity transfer is valid if R=\Gamma^{[-1]} is positive semidefinite, because the Schur product theorem sends N\ge0 to R\circ N\ge0.

If the anomaly kernel \Gamma is also positive semidefinite after normalization, then every 2-by-2 principal minor of \Gamma gives |\Gamma_{ij}|\le1, while every 2-by-2 principal minor of R gives |1/\Gamma_{ij}|\le1. Hence |\Gamma_{ij}|=1 for all i,j.

A positive semidefinite unit-diagonal matrix whose entries all have modulus one is rank one: each vector representative has equality in Cauchy-Schwarz with every other, so \Gamma_{ij}=e^{i(\theta_i-\theta_j)}. For real positive Wilson anomalies this reduces to \Gamma_{ij}=1 after diagonal locking.

Therefore the only boundary anomaly compatible with a valid universal same-theory OS bridge is a pre-locked diagonal congruence. Nonrank-one mixed damping, nonzero logarithmic cross-ratio, or an indefinite additive contact is not a harmless normalization issue but a genuine finite-matrix obstruction.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The closed-cone and Schur-matrix parts are finite-dimensional and valid under their hypotheses, but the hypotheses are precisely the unresolved continuum Yang-Mills trace theorem. In particular, RG compactness may control fixed-collar probes without controlling the collar OPE as reflected Wilson supports collide at t=0; a nonperturbative Wilson hairpin or cusp anomaly could violate the same-theory condition.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Reflection-Positivity Closed-Cone Topology: finite OS boundary-anomaly test

assumptions: For every cutoff pair (a,L) and every collar distance \delta>0, the regulated matrix N^{a,L,\delta}_{ij}=S_{a,L}(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j) is positive semidefinite by reflection positivity on the regulated gauge-invariant algebra.
The cutoff-removal topology is strong enough to pass each fixed-collar reflected matrix entry to the continuum limit; hence N^\delta\ge0 is valid for every fixed \delta.
The collar limit N=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}N^\delta exists entrywise for the finite list under consideration, so the closed cone of positive matrices gives N\ge0.
There is a finite boundary decomposition N=\Gamma\circ M+A, separating multiplicative Wilson renormalization effects from additive contact terms at the reflection plane.
The additive contact matrix A, if present as an independent boundary field covariance or positive OPE contribution, is positive semidefinite.
The reciprocal anomaly R=\Gamma^{[-1]} is a positive Schur multiplier whenever the positivity bridge is claimed to work uniformly from collar-positive matrices N to intended matrices M.
The anomaly kernel \Gamma is itself positive semidefinite after diagonal normalization when it is interpreted as a boundary expectation/correlation factor rather than an arbitrary formal correction.
definitions: source object: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms S_{a,L} evaluated on a fixed finite gauge-invariant half-space test list F=(F_1,...,F_n), together with collar maps T_\delta that keep all reflected products away from the time-zero plane before cutoff removal.

target object: the continuum OS matrix M_F=(S(\Theta F_i,F_j))_{i,j=1}^n on the locked gauge-invariant continuum test algebra, whose positivity is the finite-matrix form of OS positivity needed for Hilbert-space reconstruction.

controlled interface: fixed-collar regulated positivity plus RG convergence gives N_F=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\lim_{a,L} (S_{a,L}(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j)) as a positive matrix, and the trace comparison N_F=\Gamma_F\circ M_F+A_F measures exactly what is lost at the reflection plane.

same-theory condition: the embeddings of observables, individual Wilson-loop renormalizations, and collar-removal prescription are fixed before positivity is tested; only an invertible rank-one diagonal congruence already included in that normalization is allowed, while pair-dependent boundary counterterms, algebra enlargement, or new plane-supported observables are disallowed.
Schur product convention: for matrices B,C of the same size, B\circ C is the entrywise product, and \Gamma^{[-1]} denotes the entrywise reciprocal on a nonvanishing anomaly matrix.
Diagonal lock: the individual boundary limits have already been identified with the intended continuum observables, so N_{ii}=M_{ii} and any remaining anomaly has normalized diagonal one.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Compute a reflected Wilson-pair collar limit after individual loop renormalizations. If one finds a normalized real damping 0<\widehat\Gamma_{ij}<1, or a nonzero logarithmic cross-ratio \Delta_{ik;j\ell}\log\Gamma, then this is a falsifier: the collar-positive matrix N may be positive while the intended same-theory OS matrix M is not certified positive.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma isolates the only nonformal part of the RG-to-OS bridge at the reflection plane. The fixed-collar passage is a valid closed-cone argument; the remaining issue is whether Wilson collar collapse creates A or a nonrank-one \Gamma. Under the stated finite-matrix assumptions, positivity transfers from N to M by Schur multiplication, and the allowed multiplicative anomaly collapses to a pre-existing diagonal normalization.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Finite OS boundary-anomaly elimination lemma. Fix a finite list of gauge-invariant positive-time observables F_1,...,F_n and collar approximants T_\delta F_i supported a distance \delta>0 from the reflection plane. Suppose the fixed-collar continuum passage gives positive OS matrices N^\delta and a positive limit N, and suppose the collar-to-plane boundary value has the finite-matrix form N=\Gamma\circ M+A, where M_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i,F_j) is the intended same-theory OS matrix, \Gamma is a nonzero Hermitian multiplicative boundary anomaly, and A is an additive boundary contact matrix. If diagonal trace continuity is locked, A is a positive boundary-contact kernel, and the multiplicative correction needed to recover M from N is a valid Schur-positive reciprocal multiplier, then M\ge0. Moreover, if the anomaly kernel itself is positive after diagonal normalization, then \Gamma is only a rank-one diagonal congruence; after the pre-locked individual Wilson renormalizations it becomes \Gamma=J, so no nonfactorizing mixed Wilson damping can remain.

assumptions: The anomaly is real positive after diagonal normalization, as expected for a multiplicative damping factor in Euclidean Wilson-loop correlations.
For every sufficiently small \epsilon, the anomaly kernel and the reciprocal Schur correction are both claimed to be positive semidefinite on the finite list.
The o(\epsilon^\alpha) remainder is uniform on the finite list.
definitions: \epsilon is a collar or smoothing scale measuring how reflected Wilson supports approach the time-zero plane.
B_{ij} is the leading pair-dependent coefficient in the boundary OPE/renormalization factor after all individual loop counterterms are removed.
The test is local in scale: it only probes the first nontrivial coefficient of the mixed boundary anomaly, not the full nonperturbative Wilson expectation.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A one-loop or small-collar computation producing B_{ij}>0 for a reflected hairpin/cusp Wilson pair is a falsifier of the claimed same-theory Schur bridge.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This gives a practical perturbative search criterion for the Wilson sector: before proving a full boundary trace theorem, test whether the first mixed collar coefficient vanishes after individual renormalization.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Infinitesimal Wilson anomaly test. Suppose after diagonal locking a small-collar mixed Wilson anomaly has the expansion \widehat\Gamma^{\epsilon}_{ij}=\exp(-\epsilon^\alpha B_{ij}+o(\epsilon^\alpha)) with \widehat\Gamma^{\epsilon}_{ii}=1 and real B_{ij} for i\ne j. If both \widehat\Gamma^{\epsilon} and its reciprocal are positive kernels for all sufficiently small \epsilon, then B_{ij}=0 for every i\ne j. Thus any nonzero positive leading mixed damping coefficient is already a first-order falsifier of the universal Schur-positive same-theory bridge.

assumptions: The finite anomaly decomposition N=\Gamma\circ M+A is available.
A has either been proved zero or subtracted within the same locked theory, not by adding a new boundary observable.
The entries of \Gamma do not vanish.
definitions: Universal bridge means positivity is preserved for every positive collar-limit matrix N by a positive Schur multiplier.
Actual-matrix bridge means positivity is verified only for the specific N produced by Yang-Mills dynamics.
The branch needs the universal or structurally stable bridge; isolated actual-matrix positivity does not by itself prove the OS axiom on the full test algebra.

candidate_lemmas.statement: Actual-matrix fallback lemma. If the reciprocal anomaly is not a universally positive Schur multiplier, OS positivity for a particular finite observable list can still be checked directly by the principal minors of M=\Gamma^{[-1]}\circ(N-A). This weaker check may save a specific finite list, but it no longer supplies the topology-level bridge from regulated reflection-positive forms to OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 185 converts the Wilson boundary obstruction into a sharp dichotomy. Once diagonal trace continuity is locked, a positive additive contact cannot survive: zero diagonal forces it to vanish. For multiplicative anomalies, the universal same-theory OS bridge needs the reciprocal anomaly to be a positive Schur multiplier; if the anomaly itself is a positive boundary kernel, the 2-by-2 minors force every normalized entry to have modulus one, hence the anomaly is only a rank-one diagonal congruence. Thus the real Yang-Mills task is no longer vague preservation of reflection positivity: prove that reflected Wilson collar limits have trivial/rank-one normalized boundary factors, or find a finite mixed Wilson falsifier such as damping or a nonzero log cross-ratio.
